primary_source: Richard H. Meadow and J. Mark Kenoyer, The Tiny Steatite Seals of Harappa (2000), Figure 4 specimen 18; caption on printed/PDF p15 / PDF16 identifies excavation number.
visual_audit: Manual inspection of unmodified primary drawing, rendered at 3x for context and 8x for specimen crop. No restoration predictions consulted.

observations.observation: Three separate short strokes and a diamond-like unit with an interior feature are visible.
observations.confidence: High for this drawing; not an independent photograph.
observations.interpretation: No numeric value, phonetic reading or semantic role inferred.

observations.observation: A U-like unit and a vertical stroke cluster are visible, but the drawing is densely hatched and strokes overlap the damage/texture marks. Three versus four independent strokes cannot be resolved reliably in this scan.
observations.interpretation: The middle-face count must not be transferred to this face. This drawing cannot independently verify a three-versus-four reverse-module contrast.

observations.observation: Complex incised unit and short stroke cluster, densely drawn; fine glyph identity and count not independently adjudicated.

physical_order_caution: The article explicitly states that the sequence/orientation of face texts varies when tablets are rotated. Top/middle/bottom drawing order must not be assumed to define a linguistic order.
source_grade: Excavators' primary drawing and caption; better primary photographic plates remain required for the bottom-face stroke count.
